title: OpenAI Eyes Acquisition That Could Boost Cybersecurity Business
source_used: The Crypto Times and Digital Today (both relay The Information) plus The Information public teaser; The Information is paywalled
key_facts: The Information reported on 13 Oct 2026 that OpenAI is in early talks to buy Trail of Bits, a firm that finds and fixes vulnerabilities in open-source software.
The size of the potential deal could not be learned; talks are ongoing and could fall apart, according to people familiar with the matter.
Neither OpenAI nor Trail of Bits has publicly commented.

Trail of Bits was founded in 2012; it launched Patch the Planet with OpenAI in June 2026, pairing OpenAI models such as GPT-5.5-Cyber and Codex Security with Trail of Bits engineers to produce patches for open-source projects.
The Crypto Times: the effort found hundreds of security issues and merged dozens of patches; Trail of Bits reported 37 patches merged in projects such as cURL, Python and Go.

Digital Today: OpenAI and Anthropic have competed this year over specialised AI that finds software vulnerabilities; OpenAI recently hired Dally Rajic, a former Wiz executive, as chief revenue officer.
The Information frames the deal as part of OpenAI's attempt to build a substantial cybersecurity business.
quote_evidence: OpenAI, which is trying to develop a substantial cybersecurity business, is in early talks to buy Trail of Bits, a firm that finds and fixes vulnerabilities in open-source software, according to people familiar with the matter.
The talks, reported by The Information and which remain unconfirmed by either company and could still fall through, align with OpenAI's broader push to develop a sizable cybersecurity business.
This year, OpenAI and Anthropic have competed over developing specialised AI to find software vulnerabilities.
why_it_matters_hint: OpenAI is reported to want in-house security researchers who already work with it on open-source fixes.
notes: The Information is paywalled; read the public teaser and relays by The Crypto Times and Digital Today. The Crypto Times piece also mentions an unrelated OpenAI employee arrest, not used here.
